note: HYK-153-engine-profile-2 (coder-task.md §2 P2-4/P2-5, owner wording « literal engine-name only in the config file + registered per-engine modules », taken literally): piece B 1R's E1 category (4 rows -- engine-split-rounds.mjs:35, orca-adapter.mjs:2649, seat-candidate-adapter.mjs:281/287) was itself a config-ACCESS-argument literal living in a .mjs file, not inside the config file -- that violates the owner wording just as much as a branch comparison would. This round removed the literal argument from all four call sites (role-based lookup via getEngineByRole(), or iteration over getKnownEngines() where no role maps to the engine in question) so the literal itself is gone; E1 now has zero rows and the category name stays recognized in the schema only for a future genuine case. Separately (P2-5, honesty): piece B 1R had also moved 4 rows (seat-config-inject.mjs:62/246/279, dispatch-worker-modal-check.mjs:26) from B2-TODO to E2 with zero code change, on the precedent of claude-adapter.mjs/codex-adapter.mjs/derive-claude-project-dir-cli.mjs -- but those precedent files all carry the engine name in their own filename (the actual, checkable basis an E2 registered-per-engine-module entry needs), and neither of these two files does. This round reverted those 4 rows to B2-TODO rather than inventing a new basis for the classification (see docs/HYK-153-engine-agnostic.md for the full note; each reverted row's own note links back here). Final categories present: E2 (registered per-engine modules, filename-based precedent only), E5 (out-of-layer Claude-only hooks), B2-TODO (the 4 reverted rows above). E1/E3 have zero rows. E4 (tests/fixtures) stays out of scan scope by construction.
